title: Pack the pictures and export the room
author: claude
summary: A script cleans and packs the pictures, then the room is exported as one small file.
what: A script cleans the light maps and packs them for the web, then the room is exported and shrunk into `room_v2.glb`.
why: The browser needs small, ready-to-use files, not raw Blender output.
how:
- A light clean-up removes grain from the pictures.
- The pictures are stored at a quarter of their real brightness, so bright spots do not get clipped. The web page multiplies the brightness back.
- 70% of the probe's colour cast is removed.
- Each light map is put in the file's glow slot, which carries the second set of coordinates.
- The file is shrunk: pictures resized to 2048 pixels, saved as WebP, and the 3D shapes compressed.

tech.name: GLB file
tech.plain: A compact 3D file format that web pages can load quickly.

tech.name: gltf-transform
tech.plain: Shrinks 3D files so they load fast.

tech.name: Light maps
tech.plain: Pictures of how bright each surface is, laid over the walls and floor so the browser does not have to calculate light.

tech.name: Python scripts
tech.plain: Small programs that tell Blender what to build and bake, so every step can be repeated.
